patches.old: - **Performance-contingent rewards** (rewards tied to quality of performance) are less harmful than **task-contingent rewards** (rewards simply for doing the task).
patches.new: - **How the reward is tied to the behaviour** matters, but not in a simple ranking. Meta-analytic work finds that expected tangible rewards undermine free-choice intrinsic motivation whether they are given for merely engaging in the task, for completing it, or for performing it well. A **performance-contingent** reward is the most double-edged case: it carries the strongest competence information, which can raise interest, while also exerting the strongest control, which lowers it — so its net effect depends on which aspect the person experiences more.

visual.title: Four frameworks, four jobs
visual.alt: Maslow's five-level pyramid with the deficiency needs marked; the self-determination continuum running from amotivation through external, introjected, identified and integrated regulation to intrinsic motivation; a four-step chain showing how a promised prize shifts the perceived cause of drawing outward and leaves less drawing once withdrawn; and the expectancy-value product broken into self-efficacy on one side and interest, attainment, utility and cost on the other.
visual.caption: Identified and integrated regulation are technically extrinsic and behave almost nothing like being paid — which is the whole reason the continuum exists.
